sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff, §12.3; interaction with §§5.3 and 14.1
sol.problem: §12.3 requires verification.fault_rate in every region record, including action and perm_action. The diff unconditionally requires counts to be recomputed from F_B and applies its scheduled-context requirements to a 'scheduled region'. But §5.3 explicitly gives actions no fault outcome, and §14.1 defines F_B only for an oracle's reference body. Consequently the mandatory calculation is undefined for an otherwise valid action certificate. The published conformance/fixtures/controlled-action-09/controlled.bisa supplies a concrete witness: both controlled and flip are perm_action regions, neither invokes an oracle, and their invocation budget is zero. Filling in the proposed invocation fields does not create an F_B for either action. A checker must invent an exemption or fail to discharge a valid action certificate.
sol.fix: In §12.3, change the schema to fault_rate: null | {invocation,domain,faults_by_code,undefined_excluded,layout_dependent_excluded}. State: 'The fault-rate recount and context requirements apply only to oracle records. For action and perm_action records, verification.fault_rate MUST be null and fault_rate_contexts MUST be absent. Actions have no fault outcome of their own (§5.3); each contained lifted-oracle invocation remains subject to the recount requirements in its corresponding oracle region record.' For the controlled-X fixture, both action records therefore contain fault_rate:null and no fault_rate_contexts. Alternatively retain action-shaped records, explicitly exempt them from F_B evaluation, and require faults_by_code:{} and both exclusion counts zero; I prefer null because it distinguishes inapplicability from a verified zero-fault oracle recount.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff: §12.3 fault_rate applicability

steps.claim: F_B is the lifted-oracle result. Actions, including permutation actions, have no fault outcome, while the certificate schema places a required fault_rate field on every region record.
The proposed text requires counts to be recomputed from F_B and requires context records for a scheduled region without restricting either rule to oracles.

The published controlled-action certificate contains two perm_action region records with empty fault maps. Adding the proposed invocation fields still supplies no F_B for either region; an independent checker would need to invent an action recount convention or refuse the requested recount.
The amended universal recount requirement is therefore not implementable for an existing legal certificate class without an additional normative applicability rule.

codex.fix: In §12.3, make the field 'fault_rate: <oracle recount record> | null' and state: 'F_B recounts and fault_rate_contexts apply only to regions of kind oracle. For action and perm_action, fault_rate MUST be null and fault_rate_contexts MUST be absent. This denotes no action-owned fault outcome; it does not assert that nested oracle invocations are fault-free. Nested oracle recounts retain their own invocation/context bindings.' The corrected controlled-action fixture has fault_rate:null on both perm_action records. Alternatively, retain an explicitly defined empty action placeholder that is never evaluated through F_B and never discharges a callee obligation; I recommend null because it distinguishes inapplicability from a verified zero-fault recount.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff: §12.3 exclusion accounting; supporting claim of existing validation
codex.problem: The premise 'existing independently validated exclusion classes' is unsupported by the cited ISA text. §12.3 only names undefined_excluded and layout_dependent_excluded; §§12.1–12.2 and 14.1 do not define classification evidence, its invocation/domain binding, or an independent exclusion-validation procedure. The proposed 'enumerated applicable domain count' also leaves unclear whether excluded tuples remain in the F_B recount. North Star §5.1 excludes these inputs from native comparison while retaining reference validation. This finding concerns the proposal's false claim of existing coverage, not a demand to redesign unrelated accepted text.
codex.fix: Replace that language in §12.3 with: 'faults_by_code counts nonzero code(F_B) over every element of the declared §12.2 domain. Native-comparison exclusions do not remove elements from this reference recount. Exclusion counters MUST be independently reproduced from classification evidence bound to the same materialized program, invocation and domain. The default validation procedure replays the identified classifiers and input mapping over that domain. Missing replayable classification evidence makes the exclusion report unchecked and discharges no exclusion-dependent acceptance obligation; it MUST NOT be interpreted as zero exclusions.' State in the note that ISA 0.9 currently provides the counter names, not this validation contract. For example, if 64 of the witness's 256 tuples are independently classified as undefined, B=1 still reports faults_by_code={"1":"256"}, with undefined_excluded=64 separately. Alternatively, explicitly identify exclusion validation as an unresolved dependent contract and limit this repair's verification claim to the full-domain F_B recount; I recommend adding the obligation and default procedure here.
